quarterly_data.signal: Record quarter that beat guidance on core revenue, core gross margin and core operating margin (CFO): 'Core revenue was $209.9 million, up 103% year-over-year.' 'Core cloud and other services revenue was $127.7 million, up 287% year-over-year' ('nearly fourfold', reflecting the OpenAI deployment ramp and other cloud customers' usage); 'Core hardware revenue was $82.1 million in the quarter, up 17% compared to last year.'
quarterly_data.figure: core revenue $209.9 million, up 103%; core cloud and other services $127.7 million, up 287%; core hardware $82.1 million, up 17%

quarterly_data.signal: Margins (CFO): core gross margin 40.6% (approximately 940 basis points above Q2 2025) vs 46.5% in Q1 2026 - the sequential drop is from renting back its own systems from cloud customers; without it margins 'would have been approximately 500 basis points higher'. Core cloud and other services gross margin 41.8% (1,600 basis points better YoY); core hardware gross margin 38.8%. 'We expect Q3 to be the low point for core gross margin before improving significantly in Q4 2026' as owned, lower-cost systems replace rented ones; margin to trend toward 60% plus in 2027, helped by higher pricing, 20X throughput roadmap, 5 nm wafer cost and no HBM exposure. Core operating loss $33.6 million; core operating margin negative 16% vs negative 42% a year ago.
quarterly_data.figure: core gross margin 40.6%; cloud gross margin 41.8%; hardware gross margin 38.8%; rent-back cost approximately 500 basis points; core operating margin negative 16%

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised (CFO): Q3 2026 core revenue $214 million-$216 million, core gross margin 38%-40%, core operating margin -25% to -23%. Full year 2026 core revenue raised to $880 million-$890 million, core gross margin raised to 41%-43%, core operating margin raised to -19% to -17%. 2027: 'we expect to more than triple our core revenues in 2027 and continue to grow at multiples in the years following'; 'well-positioned to grow revenue by more than 3x in 2027'. OpenAI expected to remain 'a meaningful portion of our revenue' next year but shrink as a percentage over time.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 core revenue $214 million-$216 million; FY2026 core revenue $880 million-$890 million; FY gross margin 41%-43%; 2027 revenue more than 3x

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog (CFO): 'Remaining performance obligations at June 30, 2026, are $25.4 billion.' CEO: 'our $25 billion in RPO does not reflect any backlog of business from AWS or any other hyperscaler at this time.' Outside OpenAI and hyperscalers: 'in Q2, we signed six deals north of $30 million'; new coding customers Figma, Cognition and a 'major win at Lovable'; agentic customers Block, AlphaSense and GSK; security win with CrowdStrike. CFO: 'several late-stage hardware deals representing hundreds of millions of dollars in the pipeline from new customers, as well as significant new cloud deals for 2027'. Other hyperscaler discussions 'going well' with first revenues expected 'starting in mid-2027'; neoclouds expected to be 'an important part of our business' in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $25.4 billion at June 30, 2026; six deals north of $30 million

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build-out: 'over the last seven months, we have secured more than 600 MW of data center capacity that is either live now or will be delivered by the end of 2027', with data centers up or under contract in Alabama, Dallas, Denver, Minneapolis, Santa Clara, Stockton, France, Finland, Manitoba, Montreal, Norway, Saskatchewan and Toronto; pipeline 'now measured in gigawatts'. 'data center space continues to be the bottleneck for the entire industry, and we are no exception.' CFO: much lower net capex per megawatt than most AI clouds because Cerebras deploys its own hardware 'at much lower BOM cost that does not include the high profit margins many others must pay' and is 'reimbursed for a meaningful portion of the remaining CapEx for data center fit-out' via pass-through from its largest customer. Cash and investments of more than $8.6 billion; $850 million revolver unused.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 600 MW of data center capacity secured; more than $8.6 billion cash

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and manufacturing: 'TSMC has once again come through, and we have the wafers needed to fuel our growth' - wafer supply positioned 'not just for the remainder of this year, but for the next year as well' (CFO); 5 nm node where 'wafers are less expensive and supply is less constrained'; 'we don't use HBM memory, CoWoS packaging, or require 3 nm fab capacity'. Manufacturing capacity is 'already 4 times above where we were in the first half of 2025' and will increase 'more than 10x in 2026', with new factories being built with Flex and Sanmina; 'We already have contracted facilities three or four times more for growth in 2027'.
quarterly_data.figure: manufacturing capacity 4 times above 1H 2025; more than 10x increase in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Roadmap: CS-4 (fourth-generation system) to be unveiled 'Next week at our annual Supernova conference'; 'on track to launch our CS-5 in the second half of 2027'; new systems to 'double our speed each year for the next several years' and deliver solutions that 'increase throughput by more than 20x' over the next 18 months (CFO: quadruple current speed through end of 2027). Disaggregated inference with GPUs 'running in our labs right now... deployed and available in Q4'. Longer term: 'significant partnerships with the U.S. government for delivery of stacked memory solutions, as well as integrated wafer scale optical solutions'.
quarterly_data.figure: throughput up more than 20x over 18 months; CS-5 in the second half of 2027
